title: Refactor press transitions and theming fallback for chained buttons
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket refactors how we compute and apply press/hover/focus transitions for sequences of adjacent buttons (eg. compound actions, icon+primary, pill groups) and establishes a deterministic theming fallback when token aliases are missing or partially overridden. Recent regressions caused inconsistent elevation and color pops when disabled or loading states occur in chained button groups; this effort aims to unify the interaction model and provide a migration path for deprecated tokens.
context:
- Multiple regressions reported in console and product: hover glow flicker when adjacent icon button switches to loading; focus ring clipping when ghost button sits next to a primary pill; disabled opacity mismatch across themes.
- Root cause: token aliasing changes during last token migration introduced conditional fallbacks that resolve differently depending on DOM order and CSS specificity. Additionally, some CSS transition stacks are not isolation-safe which allows sibling state changes to trigger repaints.
- Goal: produce a resilient, theme-agnostic contract for chained buttons so interaction states are predictable and accessible across themes and sizes.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce a tiny, explicitly-namespaced 'interaction-surface' token set that decouples pressed/hover/focus elevation and overlay color from per-variant color tokens. 2) Implement a defensive resolution layer in the component which: prefers explicit token -> falls back to theme anchored alias -> falls back to neutral interaction token. 3) Replace sibling-dependent CSS transitions with an isolation layer (transform + will-change + pointer-events adjustments) and a micro-state debounce so rapid sibling updates don't produce visible jitter. 4) Add a short migration guide and codemod to surface deprecated tokens during dev build.
engineering_notes: Work with ENG runtime and frontend infra: ENG will expose kernel for micro-animation control (prefers transform over opacity where feasible). Need a Unit test harness for rendering focus ring clipping and snapshot tests for theming permutations. Plan to ship a small runtime flag to enable defensive resolution during rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Chained buttons show no visual flicker when adjacent sibling enters loading state (manual QA + 3 theme snapshots)
Disabled state opacity across all variants matches token contract within 2% contrast delta (automated color assertions)
Focus ring is not clipped in compound groups at small sizes (a11y keyboard test pass)
Token fallback resolution order documented in DS guide and implemented in component codepath

decision_log: Adopt 'interaction-surface' namespace rather than extending existing variant tokens (decision rationale: isolates interaction logic from color tokens and simplifies migration)
Use transform-based micro animations as default; opacity permitted only for overlay fades (decision rationale: avoids layout repaints and sibling repaint cascades)
Ship fallback resolution in component code instead of core CSS variables so we can roll out behind feature flag (decision rationale: safer rollout and easier telemetry)
Include codemod to annotate deprecated tokens in codebase (decision rationale: reduce developer friction during migration)
